correctness.rationale: The full tree incidence matrix has Gram determinant n; removing an edge produces a two-component forest with exactly a(n-a) nonzero signed unit maximal minors, giving each facet area sqrt(a(n-a)). Star and nonstar minima follow from the strictly increasing cut kernel up to n/2. The branch-transfer lemma changes only split sizes s to s+a with strict inequality n>2s+a and lowers the number of leaves. Each nonpath transfers strictly toward a three-leaf tripod, and two exact arm-transfer identities force arm lengths (1,1,n-3). The two gap identities follow from symmetry f(k)=f(n-k). A standalone exact integer Gram checker was actually run and passed 136 Gram/boundary checks across all unlabeled orders four through seven. Finite work is corroborative only; proof covers every n>=4.

Padrol–Pilaud–Poullot, arXiv:2111.12422, §1.3 and Theorem 2.6 concern graphical zonotope definitions and deformation cones, not sharp surface-area orderings.

value.rationale: A natural Euclidean boundary invariant distinguishes a family of all cubical graphical zonotopes of identical volume and mean width. Beyond a routine cut determinant, the result gives unique second-best and second-worst tree structures for all dimensions, exactly identical positive stability gaps at both extremes, and an asymptotic path/star factor growing as (pi/8)sqrt(n). The optimization requires a nontrivial strict branch-transfer argument and complete tripod classification.
